findings.reason: as written the worker adopts a reader that cannot express the second case of the done-when, so the first promotion a figure review meets would still be judged by code measures unless a figure-item reader is named or built.
findings.text: §25's Deliverable says the delivery check reads a record's measures "through the same reader `crew check --review` uses" and that a figure review is incomplete when it lacks a figure measure, but that reader is `review_record_refusals` (`reckon/crew/review.py`:949-962), which for a figure-rubric record skips the whole scores check — it names no figure item at all — so a figure record missing `legibility` is already accepted today and would still be accepted after the section is built; the only measure list that exists for a figure is `FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS` (`reckon/crew/review.py`:394-401), which no reader consumes

findings.reason: without a fixed key for the six verdicts the test must invent one, and the reader the section builds would then agree with its own invention rather than with the records figure reviews actually store, so the case can pass while the real promotion path stays broken.
findings.text: §25's first two cases require "a figure-review record carrying the six figure measures" and one "missing a figure measure", but the record's shape fixes no place for them: the figure prompt tells a reviewer to omit `scores` and to put "the rubric verdicts and findings in the shape above", where that shape is `RUBRIC <item>: <verdict>` report lines and a finding's four fields (`reckon/crew/prompts/figure_review.md`:22-30, 68-75), and `FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS` (`reckon/crew/review.py`:394-401) is read by nothing

findings.reason: a worker confined to the declared write paths can only duplicate the measure rule inside the delivery check (a second implementation of one truth) or stop blocked for a scope change, so the write paths must include whichever module the plan means the rubric-aware reader to live in.
findings.text: §25's write paths are `reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py` and the new test, but the completeness rule it must change is owned elsewhere: `_review_missing_measures` and `_review_is_complete` live in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py`:1501-1530, whose own docstring says the rule "has one owner", and the alternative reader lives in `reckon/crew/review.py`; the delivery module only imports the rule (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py`:674-679)
